Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, learned counsel 
for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Yogesh Chandra Tewari and Mr. 
Devendra Pant, learned Standing Counsel 
for the State of Uttarakhand/respondents.
3. By means of this writ petition, 
petitioner has challenged the order dated 
22.07.2024 passed by the Court of 
Learned Kumaon Commissioner, Kumaon
Mandal, Nainital in Appeal No.3/22-23 
Vikram Singh Vs. State through District 
Magistrate as well as order dated 
17.04.2023, passed by the Court of 
Learned District Magistrate, District Udham 
Singh Nagar, under Section 17 of Arms Act 
in Case No.52/02 of 2022 State vs. Vikram 
Singh (Annexure Nos.2 & 3).
4. Learned State Counsel prays for and is 
granted six weeks’ time to file counter 
affidavit.
5. Two weeks’ time, thereafter, is 
granted to petitioner to file rejoinder 
affidavit.
6. Put up on 12.12.2024.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.2758 of 2024
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Anil Dabral, learned Additional C.S.C. along with 
Mr. Devendra Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
3. Delay in filing the counter affidavit is condoned for the 
reasons stated in the affidavit. Delay condonation application 
(IA No.1/2025) thus stands disposed of. Counter affidavit
filed on behalf of the State is taken on record.
4. Learned State Counsel submits that he wants to file 
the SOP issued by the Central Government regarding the 
deposit of arms licenses, subject to the provisions of 
Section 24-A of the Arms Act, 1959.
5. He may submit the SOP along with supplementary 
affidavit within three weeks.
6. List on 13.10.2025.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPMS No.2758 of 2024
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Basant Singh, learned counsel i/b Mr. Harshpal 
Sekhon, learned counsel for the petitioner for the 
petitioner. 
2. Mr. Devendra Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State.
3. Learned State Counsel pursuant to order dated 
8.9.2025 has brought the SOP issued by the Central Govt. 
regarding deposit of Arms Licence, as required by this 
Court, but from a perusal of the said SOP, it is argued by 
learned State Counsel that there is no requirement for 
depositing the Arms Licence. However, the learned 
Standing Counsel submits that there may be some 
notification issued under Section 24-A of the Arms Act, 
1959. He seeks time to bring the notification on record. 
He would file the SOP as well as the notification issued 
u/s 24-A of the Act along with the supplementary affidavit 
within three weeks.
4. List on 26.11.2025.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 13.10.2025 R.Dang
